panels.description: Instant snapshot. Sources first, then sinks. See the panels to the right for the same flows plotted over time.
panels.title: Energy Flow Snapshot

panels.description: Mirror view of power flow. Sources (solar, battery discharge, grid import) stack above zero; sinks (house, charger, battery charging, grid export) stack below zero. Each side should be roughly symmetrical when the site is in balance.
panels.title: Energy Flow — Sources ↑ / Sinks ↓

panels.description: Stacked inputs over time: roof PV, balcony PV, battery discharge and grid import. The total area equals total instantaneous demand.
panels.title: Sources — Where the Power Comes From

panels.description: Stacked outputs over time: house load, EV charger, battery charging and grid export.
panels.title: Sinks — Where the Power Goes

panels.description: 6-hour moving average of power flows (5 min buckets, 72-point window). Smooths out short spikes to show sustained trends. Sources above zero, sinks below.
panels.title: Energy Flow — 6h Moving Average (Sources ↑ / Sinks ↓)

panels.description: Everything above zero. Solar generation (roof + balcony) stacked as a filled area; consumption (house + charger + battery charging) stacked as line bands on top. Wherever the solar fill exceeds the consumption lines, the surplus went to the battery or back to the grid.
panels.title: Solar Generation vs. Consumption (both stacked ↑)

panels.description: Raw PV generation split by source before any Solarbank buffering or battery discharge contribution.
panels.title: PV Breakdown
